major_features: Custom relational algebra parser converting SQL projections, selections, and inner joins into explicit AST nodes
Memoization table architecture storing equivalent logical and physical expression trees with shared sub-plans
Rule-based transformation engine supporting predicate pushdown, constant folding, and join reordering
Cost-based exploration framework utilizing catalog statistics histograms to score physical execution plans
Dynamic programming join-order enumerator implementing Left-Deep and Bushy tree search spaces
Volcano-style property enforcer ensuring required sort orders and physical distribution traits are met
Plan visualizer generating hierarchical string representations and structural cost breakdowns for debugging
Deterministic verification harness validating optimizer output stability against mutated cardinality inputs
candidate_ideas.name: OmniQuery Planner
candidate_ideas.pain: Database engineers cannot easily inspect how relational algebra trees are transformed into execution graphs or how join-order dynamic programming behaves under different cardinality estimators.
candidate_ideas.problem: Traditional database cost-based optimizers hide their search space exploration and rewrite heuristics, making it impossible to study alternative plan generation and rule-based transformations without reading a monolithic commercial codebase.
candidate_ideas.solution: A zero-dependency relational query optimizer written in Java 21. It features a custom SQL-to-RelNode parser, Volcano/Cascades style equivalence-class rule engine, memoized search space container, and dynamic cost estimator.
candidate_ideas.target_user: Database Systems Engineers and Compiler Researchers
candidate_ideas.verification: Deterministic integration suite feeding malformed relational expressions, cyclic join graphs, and zero-cardinality catalog statistics to verify robust optimizer fallback and cost bounds exceptions.

major_features: Event timestamp extractor and watermark generator supporting punctuated and bounded-out-of-orderness heuristics
Tumbling and sliding time window aggregators maintaining incremental state without full memory recomputation
Session window operator dynamically merging active time gaps based on configurable inactivity thresholds
Stream-to-stream interval join engine evaluating temporal bounds across two distinct event feeds
In-memory state backend supporting keyed state partitions and checkpoint metadata snapshots
Late-data side-output routing mechanism capturing and diverting events arriving past watermark thresholds
Virtual Thread-based event ingestion pipeline orchestrating non-blocking source-to-sink dataflow
Deterministic unit verification suite validating aggregation correctness under shuffled event sequences
candidate_ideas.name: Titanium Stream Engine
candidate_ideas.pain: Engineers lack an isolated, zero-dependency stream processing engine that implements sliding/tumbling windows and watermarks entirely from scratch for local event-driven testing.
candidate_ideas.problem: Event stream processors often rely on massive distributed clusters and complex JVM configuration layers, preventing low-latency, single-node stream analytics with precise windowing semantics.
candidate_ideas.solution: A zero-dependency stream processing and windowing engine written in Java 21. It processes raw event streams through tumbling and sliding time windows, manages late-data watermarks, and executes stream joins in-memory.
candidate_ideas.target_user: Distributed Systems Developers and Real-Time Data Engineers
candidate_ideas.verification: Comprehensive test harness injecting out-of-order event streams, extreme clock skews, and malformed timestamp payloads to assert watermark progression and late-event side-output correctness.

major_features: Multi-dimensional tensor data structure managing contiguous and non-contiguous memory strides
Broadcasting rules engine automatically aligning shape dimensions for element-wise vector operations
Matrix multiplication kernel optimized with cache-friendly blocking and transpose caching
Dynamic computation graph tape recording operation nodes for reverse-mode automatic differentiation
Gradient accumulator managing multi-branch node accumulation and variable sharing
In-place tensor mutation checker preventing invalid gradient tracking on modified buffers
Binary serialization subsystem for saving and loading tensor weights and computation metadata
Comprehensive test harness validating gradient tape backpropagation against analytical derivatives
candidate_ideas.name: TensorCore VM
candidate_ideas.pain: Developers studying deep learning primitives cannot inspect pure, dependency-free implementations of multi-dimensional tensor slicing, contiguous memory striding, and reverse-mode automatic differentiation.
candidate_ideas.problem: Higher-level tensor libraries hide memory layout management, hardware-agnostic tensor broadcasting, and tape-based autodiff mechanics behind massive C++ runtimes, hindering direct study of numeric computation kernels.
candidate_ideas.solution: A zero-dependency multi-dimensional tensor computation engine and reverse-mode autodiff virtual machine written in Python 3.12. It implements contiguous and strided views, broadcast arithmetic, and a dynamic computation graph tape.
candidate_ideas.target_user: Machine Learning Infrastructure Engineers and Compiler Devs
candidate_ideas.verification: Rigorous verification suite comparing computed gradients against numerical finite-difference approximations across edge-case shapes, zero-stride dimensions, and NaN-injected computation graphs.

major_features: Fixed-size file page manager allocating and tracking free-space bitmap pages on disk
Slotted-page record allocator packing variable-length binary byte arrays with offset redirection pointers
Buffer pool manager implementing clock-sweep page eviction and pin/unpin concurrency locking
Binary Write-Ahead Log (WAL) recording undo/redo transaction records with CRC32 checksum verification
Crash-recovery engine scanning log files to execute ARIES-style analysis, redo, and undo phases
Record-level iterator supporting sequential page scans and point-lookup record retrieval
Virtual Thread-based asynchronous background page flusher synchronizing dirty cache blocks to disk
Deterministic test harness injecting partial writes and corrupted page headers to validate error trapping
candidate_ideas.name: Apex Storage Engine
candidate_ideas.pain: Systems engineers studying low-level storage architectures lack a modular, zero-dependency single-file database engine with custom slotted-page layouts and lock-free buffer pool management.
candidate_ideas.problem: Key-value stores often couple storage layout directly to networking protocols, making it difficult to analyze pure page cache management, buffer pool eviction, and crash-safe WAL recovery in isolation.
candidate_ideas.solution: A zero-dependency disk-based storage engine written in Java 21. It manages fixed-size data pages, a slotted-page record layout for variable-length tuples, a clock-sweep buffer pool cache, and a binary write-ahead log.
candidate_ideas.target_user: Storage Engine Architects and Database Developers
candidate_ideas.verification: Fault-injection verification harness simulating power failure mid-write, torn page segments, and buffer eviction races to confirm Write-Ahead Log recovery atomicity.

major_features: Graph-based network topology model simulating nodes, weighted edges, and duplex communication links
Path-vector routing table engine storing next-hop destinations, cost metrics, and full AS paths
Asynchronous message passing framework delivering serialized route advertisement packets between nodes
Split-horizon with poison reverse mechanism preventing routing loops on shared network segments
Link-state and distance-vector protocol state machines handling dynamic metric updates and node failures
Topology convergence detector tracking routing table stabilization epochs across network mutations
Simulated packet drop and latency injector introducing configurable network jitter and packet loss
Deterministic verification harness asserting loop-free convergence following arbitrary topology splits
candidate_ideas.name: Helix Routing Protocol
candidate_ideas.pain: Engineers cannot test custom path-vector routing protocols, split-horizon poison reverse mechanics, and convergence stability under dynamic link failure without deploying physical hardware or heavy containers.
candidate_ideas.problem: Network routing simulation tools are either overly simplified educational abstractions or massive network emulators that require root privileges and complex virtual interface configurations.
candidate_ideas.solution: A zero-dependency path-vector routing protocol simulator and network engine written in Java 21. It implements asynchronous distance-vector route exchanges, split-horizon updates, and topology convergence detection over simulated loopback channels.
candidate_ideas.target_user: Systems Engineers and Network Protocol Researchers
candidate_ideas.verification: Exhaustive simulation suite injecting network partitions, routing loops, oscillating link metrics, and malformed route advertisement packets to assert protocol stabilization and loop prevention.

known_limitations: Gemini discovery reasons from model knowledge; the factory does not claim live market research or verified market demand.

A passing systems release proves the generated source compiled or byte-compiled and its factory-required unit/integration suites passed; it does not by itself prove production-scale reliability, security certification, or benchmark superiority.
Generated systems projects intentionally use standard-library-only Java 21, C11, or Python 3.12 profiles so validation can be deterministic and does not depend on unverifiable third-party packages.

Hard projects are scoped implementations of real mechanisms, not claims of complete compatibility with Redis, full SQL standards, industrial compilers, or frontier machine-learning systems unless the tests and documentation explicitly demonstrate that scope.
